subject.title: [Bug] Orphaned/oversized native Codex thread wedges a session permanently — chat.send returns started but no run executes, silently dropping messages

question: For a persisted Codex native-thread preflight that cannot establish a runnable turn, should Gateway force a fresh native thread and retry, or fail the accepted send visibly with an operator recovery action?
rationale: Both outcomes avoid silent message loss, but they differ in context-continuity, retry semantics, and the public meaning of a successful chat-send acknowledgement.

options.title: Run-or-error admission contract
options.body: Require dispatch to confirm a durable run start or return a visible terminal error, then add a narrowly scoped recovery path for the failed native binding.

options.title: Force-rotate before failure
options.body: Attempt one fresh native-thread rotation and retry before returning a visible failure, with explicit telemetry when recovery is used.

options.title: Fail fast only
options.body: Return an actionable error without automatic rotation when native-thread preflight cannot prove the binding is safe.

recommendation.title: Run-or-error admission contract
recommendation.body: Require dispatch to confirm a durable run start or return a visible terminal error, then add a narrowly scoped recovery path for the failed native binding.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged work most directly owns the native-thread preflight and rotation boundary implicated by the report.
